item.description: La Antártida se ve como un paraje donde solo se pueden encontrar pingüinos, pero la realidad es que también es una tierra que puede llegar a fascinar a cualquier microbiólogo por la adaptación que han sufrido diferentes bacterias. item.title: How penguin poo is making Antarctic snow melt faster
item.description: Researchers find the birds’ guano feeds algal blooms that absorb significantly more solar energy Penguin poo is making the Antarctic snow melt faster, a study shows. As temperatures rise, penguins are waddling closer to the south pole, with potential for this previously unrecognised phenomenon to affect a wider area. Snow algae are tiny single-celled plants that make a home in some of the coldest places on Earth. When nutrients are scarce, the algae produces red pigments to protect itself from the sun and slow growth. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: The next global pandemic could be brewing on a mink farm in Utah – and little is being done to stop it | George Monbiot
item.description: Mink farms are the perfect petri dishes for deadly flu strains to emerge. Yet officials appear to be protecting business interests over human lives Could this be ground zero? Could it be the spot where the next pandemic begins? It’s certainly a candidate, not least because the chain of events that could trigger a plague far worse than Covid-19 looks like the opening sequence of a disaster movie. A really bad disaster movie, in which the levels of carelessness and turpitude defy belief.
